Thought: When toxic metals or metal compounds react with oxidizing acids, several hazardous reactions can occur. Let me consider each option:

A. Explosion - Yes, some metals (like alkali metals) can react violently with acids causing explosions
B. Fire - Yes, certain metal-acid reactions can generate enough heat to cause fires
C. Flammable gas generation - Yes, some metals (like zinc) produce hydrogen gas when reacting with acids, which is flammable
D. Heat generation - Yes, metal-acid reactions are typically exothermic
E. Innocuous and non-flammable gas generation - No, the gases produced are typically hazardous
F. May be hazardous but unknown - This is too vague when we know specific hazards
G. Solubilization of toxic substance - Yes, acids can dissolve toxic metals, creating toxic solutions
H. Toxic gas generation - Yes, certain metal compounds (like sulfides) can generate toxic gases (like H2S) when mixed with acids
I. Violent polymerization - No, polymerization is not typically associated with metal-acid reactions

Based on my analysis, the correct answers are A (Explosion), B (Fire), C (Flammable gas generation), D (Heat generation), G (Solubilization of toxic substance), and H (Toxic gas generation).
